# Base image with OpenMPI, Flux, and EFA support for AWS on ARM64
FROM ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-openmpi:ubuntu2204-efa-arm

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, clone LAMMPS, build with REAXFF package, install, and clean up
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    wget && \
    # Create a temporary build directory
    mkdir -p /tmp/build && \
    cd /tmp/build && \
    # Clone the latest version of the LAMMPS source code
    git clone https://github.com/lammps/lammps.git && \
    cd lammps && \
    mkdir build && cd build && \
    # Configure the build with CMake
    # - BUILD_MPI=yes: Enable MPI support for multi-node execution
    # - PKG_REAXFF=yes: Include the ReaxFF package as requested
    # - CMAKE_C_COMPILER/CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER: Use the MPI wrappers from the base image
    # - CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX: Set the installation path for binaries
    cmake -D CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/usr/local \
          -D BUILD_MPI=yes \
          -D PKG_REAXFF=yes \
          -D CMAKE_C_COMPILER=mpicc \
          -D CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=mpicxx \
          ../cmake && \
    # Compile using all available processor cores
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    # Install the 'lmp' executable to /usr/local/bin, which is on the system PATH
    make install && \
    # Create the final working directory for the application
    mkdir -p /opt/lammps-reax && \
    # Copy the required example files to the working directory
    cp /tmp/build/lammps/examples/reaxff/HNS/* /opt/lammps-reax/ && \
    # Clean up the build directory and package cache to reduce image size
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /tmp/build && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Verify that the LAMMPS executable is in the system PATH
RUN which lmp

# Set the default working directory for the container
WORKDIR /opt/lammps-reax

# Set a default command to start a shell
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

# This MiniCluster manifest is designed for running an HPC application (LAMMPS)
# on an AWS ARM-based CPU cluster with EFA networking, managed by the Flux Operator.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster job
  name: lammps-reax-aws-cpu
  # The namespace to deploy to
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster, corresponding to nodes.
  size: 4

  # The total number of MPI tasks to run across all pods.
  tasks: 16

  # Keep pods after the job finishes for debugging and log inspection.
  cleanup: false

  # Enable strict mode for logging, which provides more detailed output.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Flux Framework specific configurations
  flux:
    # Specify the architecture for ARM instances.
    arch: "arm"

    # Flux container settings
    container:
      # Use the ARM-specific image for the Flux view.
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-ubuntu:arm-jammy

      # Since Flux is expected to be included in the main application container,
      # we disable the automatic injection of the Flux sidecar container.
      disable: true

  # Define the main application container
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
      imagePullPolicy: Always

      # The command to be executed by Flux. The `flux run` prefix is added automatically by the operator.
      # This runs the LAMMPS simulation with the specified input file and variables.
      command: lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite

      # This is the main application container, not a launcher pod.
      launcher: false

      # Resource requests and limits required for AWS Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA).
      # This ensures the pod is scheduled on a node with an available EFA device.
      resources:
        limits:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: "1"
        requests:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: "1"

# This MiniCluster manifest is designed for running an HPC application (LAMMPS)
# on a single AWS ARM-based CPU node with EFA networking, managed by the Flux Operator.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: lammps-reax-aws-cpu
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster, set to 1 for single-node testing.
  size: 1
  # The total number of MPI tasks to run. Corresponds to the new command parameters (2*2*2=8).
  tasks: 8

  # Do not retry the job on failure.
  backoffLimit: 1

  # Keep pods after the job finishes for debugging and log inspection.
  cleanup: false

  # Enable strict mode for logging, which provides more detailed output.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Pod-specific configurations are nested under the 'pod' field.
  pod:
    # Set the restart policy to Never, which is typical for batch jobs.
    restartPolicy: Never
    # Add a nodeSelector to ensure pods are scheduled on specific AWS instance types.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: m7g.16xlarge

  # Flux Framework specific configurations
  flux:
    # Specify the architecture for ARM instances.
    arch: arm
    # Add Flux option flags to control CPU affinity for each task.
    optionFlags: -o cpu-affinity=per-task
    # Flux container settings
    container:
      # Use the ARM-specific image for the Flux view.
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-ubuntu:arm-jammy
      # Since Flux is expected to be included in the main application container,
      # we disable the automatic injection of the Flux sidecar container.
      disable: true

  # Define the main application container
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
      imagePullPolicy: Always

      # The command to be executed by Flux for a smaller, single-node test case.
      command: lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite

      # This is the main application container, not a launcher pod.
      launcher: false

      # Resource requests and limits required for AWS Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA).
      # This ensures the pod is scheduled on a node with an available EFA device.
      resources:
        limits:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: "1"
        requests:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: "1"

apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: lammps-reax-aws-cpu
  namespace: default
spec:
  backoffLimit: 1
  cleanup: false
  containers:
  - command: lmp -v x 24 -v y 12 -v z 12 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite
    image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
    imagePullPolicy: Always
    launcher: false
    resources:
      limits:
        vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: '1'
      requests:
        vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: '1'
  flux:
    arch: arm
    container:
      disable: true
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-ubuntu:arm-jammy
    optionFlags: -o cpu-affinity=per-task
  logging:
    strict: true
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: m7g.16xlarge
    restartPolicy: Never
  size: 4
  tasks: 256

manager.name: Build and Deploy LAMMPS
manager.description: Build a Docker container and deploy it as a Kubernetes Job.

context.environment: AWS CPU instance in Kubernetes to run across nodes
context.details:
You MUST use ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-openmpi:ubuntu2204-efa-arm as a base image. It includes OpenMPI and libfabric provided from the efa installer for AWS and the entire Flux Framework stack.
You MUST compile lammps setting the cxx compiler to mpicxx and the c compiler to mpicc.
Ensure all globbed files from examples/reaxff/HNS from the root of the lammps codebase are in the WORKDIR. Clone the latest branch of LAMMPS. You MUST put lmp on the PATH and run which lmp to ensure success.
You MUST build LAMMPS for a multi-node MPI environment

context.optimize:
You MUST maximize the LAMMPS FOM, *atom steps per second.  It could be Matom or katom.
You MUST parse a result to include the units for katom or Matom.
You MUST choose the largest problem size to maximize FOM. You MAY go up to 4 nodes. 
You MUST make an effort to increase problem size as much as you can.
You MUST set flux.optionFlags to "-o cpu-affinity=per-task"
You can use lmp -v x 24 -v y 12 -v z 12 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite to start on 4 nodes (FOM of 2.094 Matom)
context.resources: The resource spec you got earlier is for an autoscaling cluster, so the nodes possible are not there. You must add the nodeSelector to use node.kubernetes.io/instance-type m7g.16xlarge with 64 CPU, 256 GiB Memory, ARM (Graviton3). You are limited to up to 4 nodes.
context.testing: Run in.reaxff.hns in the pwd with lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite for testing only on all processes of one node.
context.details:
You MUST run on up to 4 nodes and you MUST set flux.container.disable to true.
You MUST set the containers imagePullPolicy to Always.
The Flux Operator uses flux run in the pwd with the tasks determined by the spec.tasks.
You MUST set resource requests and limits to use vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: 1
Since this is an ARM instance you MUST change the flux.container.image to be
ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-ubuntu:arm-jammy and set flux.arch: "arm".
